## Purpose and public entry points
SAM 3 is a Python/PyTorch foundation-model package for promptable image and video instance segmentation: text, points, boxes, masks, and visual exemplars drive detection, segmentation, and tracking. Primary API construction is in `sam3/model_builder.py`; image callers use `sam3/model/sam3_image_processor.py`, while video callers use the request/session interface in `sam3/model/sam3_video_predictor.py`.

## Model assembly and shared representation
The builder loads authorized Hugging Face checkpoints and composes the model variants. A shared vision backbone produces image features, then model-specific layers consume them. Core representation and model primitives reside in:
- `sam3/model_builder.py`
- `sam3/model/encoder.py`
- `sam3/model/vitdet.py`

The material runtime is Python 3.12+, PyTorch 2.7+, and a CUDA 12.6+ compatible GPU; optional FlashAttention 3 and custom connected-components extensions accelerate inference.

## Detector: prompt-conditioned image segmentation
The image path prepares an input image into inference state, encodes text/geometry/visual prompts, runs a DETR-like detector, and returns masks, boxes, and confidence scores. The detector is deliberately separated from temporal tracking:
- `sam3/model/sam3_image_processor.py`
- `sam3/model/sam3_image.py`
- `sam3/model/sam3_multiplex_detector.py`

Text is tokenized and encoded before multimodal fusion; image-exemplar and geometric prompts enter through the same detector-facing boundary:
- `sam3/model/tokenizer_ve.py`
- `sam3/model/text_encoder_ve.py`
- `sam3/model/vl_combiner.py`

## Tracker and video session control
Video inference is stateful: a client starts a session from an MP4 or JPEG-frame resource, adds or refines prompts on arbitrary frames, and receives propagated object outputs. The predictor owns request dispatch and session lifecycle; base/tracking layers preserve per-object temporal state:
- `sam3/model/sam3_video_predictor.py`
- `sam3/model/sam3_video_inference.py`
- `sam3/model/sam3_tracking_predictor.py`

SAM 3.1 adds multiplex tracking: multiple objects share memory for faster joint tracking, separated from the detector implementation:
- `sam3/model/sam3_multiplex_video_predictor.py`
- `sam3/model/sam3_multiplex_tracking.py`
- `sam3/model/video_tracking_multiplex.py`

## Segmentation and memory boundary
The tracker inherits a SAM-style transformer encoder/decoder and mask decoder. Prompt encoding, memory reads/writes, and mask decoding form the core boundary between interactive prompts and temporal propagation:
- `sam3/sam/prompt_encoder.py`
- `sam3/sam/mask_decoder.py`
- `sam3/model/memory.py`

## Agent orchestration
An optional agent decomposes complex language requests and coordinates an external LLM with SAM 3 image inference. This is an integration boundary rather than a required core inference path:
- `sam3/agent/agent_core.py`
- `sam3/agent/client_llm.py`
- `sam3/agent/client_sam3.py`

## Training and evaluation
Training feeds COCO-style image/video datasets through transforms, matching, segmentation losses, distributed training, and checkpointing:
- `sam3/train/train.py`
- `sam3/train/trainer.py`
- `sam3/train/data/sam3_video_dataset.py`

Evaluation converts predictions into benchmark formats and computes image, video, and tracking metrics, including SA-Co VEval and bundled HOTA/TETA toolkits:
- `sam3/eval/saco_veval_eval.py`
- `sam3/eval/coco_eval.py`
- `sam3/eval/hota_eval_toolkit/eval.py`

Checkpoint and benchmark data are external: model weights require Hugging Face access; SA-Co datasets are hosted on Hugging Face and Roboflow.
